Given ^s, we estimate ₁ by unrolling the Lanczos algorithm and use sign(₁) for binary classification. Mathematically, we develop a theorem establishing conditions under which ₁ can be well approximated after finite Lanczos iterations. Motivated by this theorem, we relax the classical Lanczos orthogonality constraints during unrolling and optimize end-to-end classification performance while promoting the derived conditions for accurate eigenvector approximation. Experiments on real-world Harmonized Landsat-Sentinel imagery show classification performance comparable to state-of-the-art deep learning models while reducing parameters by up to two orders of magnitude.

entries.title: Risk-Aware Joint Inference and Resource Control for Physical AI in 6G Networks
entries.abstract: Wireless edge inference enables Physical-AI devices to execute edge-inferred actions using transmitted sensory inputs. Since the risk of incorrect actions vary across observations and tasks, the associated uplink transmission of sensory inputs requires different levels of wireless reliability. For instance, applying a fixed signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) requirement can overprovision low-risk tasks while underprovisioning high-risk ones. Therefore, we propose risk-aware control for edge inference (RACE), which maps predicted action-failure probability and task criticality to adaptive SINR targets and combines them with deadline-derived SINR requirements. A slow-timescale large language model (LLM) proposes task requirements for deterministic validation, while a fast hybrid actor selects inference configurations and transmit power levels, complemented by analytical receive beamforming and finite power restoration. Simulations show 11% improvement in the average accuracy-latency-energy objective over fixed-high-SINR control, with near-zero constraint outage.
entries.comment: Submitted to IEEE for possible publication

entries.title: Cascading Contingency Analysis of Modern Power Systems Using a Stochastic Hybrid Systems Framework
entries.abstract: This paper presents a cascading contingency analysis and risk assessment framework that incorporates probabilistic mode transitions motivated by stochastic hybrid system (SHS) concepts together with power-flow-based stress evaluation. A two-stage modeling approach is adopted in which sensitivity-based analysis is first used to identify candidate cascading transitions, followed by DC power flow re-evaluation to accurately capture post-contingency stress redistribution, islanding behavior, and load shedding. A probabilistic propagation model is constructed using mode-dependent transition probabilities derived from line loading conditions. A Cascading Risk Index (CRI) is introduced to quantify the expected load shedding accumulated over cascade progression. Case studies on the IEEE 39-bus system demonstrate that the proposed framework captures diverse cascading routes under multiple initiating outages and identifies critical propagation patterns that are not revealed by N-1/N-2 screening. The results highlight the importance of SHS modeling in assessing cascading risk and providing a scalable framework for resilience evaluation in modern power systems.
entries.comment: This paper was accepted at the 2026 North American Power Symposium (NAPS)

entries.title: Achieving Robust Channel Estimation Neural Networks on Doppler effects by Designed Training Data
entries.abstract: Channel estimation is crucial in wireless communication systems. Many existing works train and test their models using the same or similar channel. However, practical channels are infinitely diverse and time-variant while data-driven algorithms often degrade on new and previously unseen channels. This prohibits the practical implementation of neural networks for channel estimation, particularly in high speed scenarios characterized by rapidly channel profile changes and very high Doppler shifts. Online training can fine-tune models to adapt to new channels, but requires high computation resource and incurs significant latency for physical-layer devices. Moreover, online training cannot exhaustively cover all possible channels because there are infinitely many possible channels. Therefore, we investigate the ability of neural networks to generalize to wireless channels. This paper proposes design criteria to generate synthetic training data, which guaranty that the resulting networks perform robustly across wireless channels, especially for very high Doppler shifts and different Doppler spectra. It ensures that offline-trained neural networks require no prior information or online training to precisely estimate the new channels. To demonstrate general applicability, we use neural networks with different levels of complexity to show that the generalization achieved appears to be independent of architecture. From simulation results, neural networks achieve a certain performance across wireless channels with different unseen power delay profiles (PDP) and Doppler shifts.

entries.title: Physics-Constrained Autoencoder for Interpretable Health Representation Learning in Turbofan Engines
entries.abstract: Health Indices (HIs) summarize degradation from operational data and support diagnostic and prognostic tasks in Prognostics and Health Management (PHM). Their usefulness depends on capturing degradation and interpreting system condition. Autoencoders learn such representations from unlabelled monitoring data; however, when training is driven only by reconstruction, the physical meaning of latent variables remains undefined, limiting their interpretation and diagnostic value. This work proposes a physics-constrained autoencoder that embeds system knowledge as an inductive bias in the decoder architecture and as a learning bias in the loss function. The decoder contains differentiable physical equations that receive latent variables and operating conditions as inputs, structurally guiding each latent variable to represent a predefined physical quantity and enabling component-level analysis before aggregation into a system-level HI.The methodology is benchmarked on the N-CMAPSS dataset against alternative representations. Reconstruction reaches an R² of 0.9993 and an MAE of 0.0036, comparable to fully data-driven models. After operating-condition correction, the inferred physical quantities track degradation, and their aggregation produces an HI with a Spearman correlation of 0.9791 with the ground truth, an RMSE of 0.0286, and an MAE of 0.0233. The methodology is further evaluated using a single model trained across four datasets representing distinct degradation scenarios. This model preserves component-level signatures that distinguish compression-side from expansion-side degradation without diagnostic labels.Finally, the proposed framework enables degradation trends to be visualized on component maps, providing a health representation in a form familiar to engine operators and domain experts.

entries.title: Chain of Physics: Supporting Fault Diagnosis with Engineering-Inspired Large Language Model Reasoning
entries.abstract: Fault diagnosis in complex systems requires linking observed changes in physical quantities to the failure mechanisms that produce them. Experienced engineers perform this task by combining sensor information with knowledge of system behavior and fault propagation. Large Language Models (LLMs) can support this process, but their diagnostic reasoning depends on the availability of asset-specific engineering knowledge and on how this knowledge is represented and used during inference. This work introduces Chain of Physics (CoP), an LLM-based fault-diagnosis framework built around a Constrained Knowledge Graph (CKG) generated automatically from asset-specific reference documentation. CoP addresses failure-sensor association from textual engineering knowledge. The CKG stores diagnostic chains connecting failure modes, changes in physical quantities, and monitoring sensors. During inference, semantically similar graph paths are retrieved for each question and used as both information and in-context examples for the reasoning process. Candidate failure modes are extracted from the question and analysed independently through dedicated LLM calls, which generate plausible failure-to-observation chains. A final decision module compares these chains with the available answer choices. CoP is evaluated on the FailureSensorIQ benchmark across four industrial asset classes and three LLMs. Compared with direct prompting and conventional Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), CoP improves diagnostic accuracy across all evaluated models, with gains ranging from 7.8 to 19.6 percentage points and from 11.7 to 18.2 percentage points, respectively. The results show that structured engineering knowledge can improve LLM-based diagnostic reasoning when graph retrieval is combined with in-context examples of fault propagation.

entries.title: CFAR Detection on Non-Coherently Integrated Angular Maps for mmWave Radio SLAM
entries.abstract: Reliable multipath detection is essential for millimeter-wave simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM), where propagation paths reflecting off the environment provide geometric constraints beyond the dominant line-of-sight component. This paper develops constant false alarm rate (CFAR)-based detectors for beam-swept bistatic integrated sensing and communications (ISAC). Starting from conventional CFAR on the I/Q datacube, we derive a modified detector for non-coherently integrated angular power maps, where the post-integration noise statistics differ from those assumed by standard cell-averaging CFAR. To improve practicality, we introduce a multi-cell cell-under-test formulation and a plus-shaped training window that reduces computational cost while accounting for sidelobe structure. The proposed methods are evaluated on experimental 60 GHz indoor measurements using a snapshot-SLAM estimator. Compared with a singular value decomposition (SVD)-based detector, the proposed CFAR approaches reduce the overall positioning RMSE from 0.30 m to 0.24-0.26 m, with the largest improvement in non-line-of-sight snapshots. The multi-cell non-coherent detector further lowers the computational complexity without degrading positioning accuracy, demonstrating its suitability for practical multipath radio-SLAM.
entries.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication

entries.title: Dual-Parabola Interpolator: A Low-Bias Peak Estimator for Distributed Radar Synchronization
entries.abstract: Coherent distributed radar processing requires accurate wireless synchronization. Two-way time transfer (TWTT) obtains reception timestamps from sampled matched-filter peaks, but interpolation bias limits accuracy even when noise is reduced by higher signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) or averaging. Three-point parabolic interpolation is attractive for its simple, explicit formula; reducing its bias generally requires more elaborate fitting, such as higher-order polynomials, or a model tailored to a particular peak shape. A practical alternative should retain this simplicity and interpretability while approaching the low bias of more flexible fits. We propose the Dual-Parabola Interpolator (DPI), which combines two parabolic estimates from five amplitude samples near the matched-filter peak. An adaptive weight cancels the leading interpolation error without requiring a waveform-specific peak model or a correction table. Simulations over flat and standardized multipath channels show bias comparable to a five-point quartic fit, with essentially the same standard deviation as the other interpolators and an execution cost close to a three-point parabolic fit. This combination is useful for TWTT in urban or other multipath settings, where channel distortion prevents reliance on a nominal peak shape.
entries.comment: 6 pages, 7 figures. Submitted for peer review as a conference paper

entries.title: Finite Blocklength Performance Analysis of Uplink RSMA with Practical Imperfections
entries.abstract: Future generations of wireless networks will support massive communication and hyper-reliable low-latency communications, which are fundamental to large-scale Internet of Things (IoT) deployments with stringent performance requirements. To support such diverse and demanding requirements, robust and flexible multiple access schemes are essential. In this work, we develop a comprehensive analytical framework for evaluating uplink rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) in the finite blocklength regime under realistic non-ideal conditions. Specifically, we derive closed-form expressions for the block error rate (BLER) and goodput, accounting for imperfect channel state information at the receiver (CSIR), imperfect successive interference cancellation (SIC), and hardware impairments. To reflect practical wireless environments, we model the channel using Nakagami-m fading model. Our analysis shows that at lower transmit power levels, imperfect CSIR is the dominant performance-limiting factor, whereas hardware impairments and imperfect SIC become more significant in degrading system performance as the transmit power increases. To further understand the system behavior, we derive asymptotic BLER expressions. We also analyze the impact of rate allocation, demonstrating its critical role in ensuring fairness and reliability. Monte Carlo simulations validate our analytical expressions. Notably, our results show that uplink RSMA significantly outperforms NOMA even when RSMA operates under harsh imperfect CSIR. This superiority establishes RSMA as a robust and efficient candidate for future wireless networks in practical, constrained environments

entries.title: ScaleBrain: A Scale-Consistent Framework for EEG Foundation Models
entries.abstract: Foundation models pre-trained on large unlabeled electroencephalography (EEG) corpora have emerged as a transformative paradigm for Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) applications. Recent EEG foundation models have shown that multi-scale representations derived from fixed-length patches can improve EEG representation learning. Existing frameworks commonly construct temporal scales through feature-level operations. However, these operations leave the correspondence between learned features and scale-specific characteristics of the original EEG signals implicit. Moreover, when the self-supervised objective is not aligned with the multi-scale input representations, information at some temporal scales may receive insufficient supervision during pre-training. In light of this, we propose ScaleBrain, a scale-consistent pre-training framework that explicitly coordinates multi-scale representations of EEG from both the model input and optimization objective sides. Specifically, ScaleBrain introduces multi-scale EEG tokenization to represent the same EEG segment through analysis windows with different temporal spans and shared temporal anchors, and pairs these representations with scale-specific reconstruction to align with the multi-scale input structure and provide supervision across temporal resolutions during self-supervised learning. We further develop an axial spatio-temporal attention mechanism to contextualize the fused multi-scale representation along spatial and temporal dimensions. Extensive evaluations on six public BCI benchmarks against 12 representative baselines show that ScaleBrain achieves the highest mean Balanced Accuracy on five datasets and ranks third on the remaining one, with only 5.0M parameters, demonstrating strong performance and favorable parameter efficiency.

entries.title: Application of the Phase Correction Method in Tracking Modules of Navigation Receivers
entries.abstract: One of the problems of the tracking modules is their significant inertia in case of narrow bandwidth, which is desirable to mitigate signal noise. The paper describes a method of phase correction, improving accuracy and dynamic characteristics of the tracking process in GNSS receivers. The pivotal idea of the method supposes correction of the phase deviation between the received signal and its local copy at the end of every integration period. This correction is performed directly over the phase accumulator of a DDS system. This approach reduces inertial effects crucially. Application of phase correction method with narrow filter bandwidth is much more efficient when FLL-assisted PLL tracking is used. It is shown that in this case a separate FLL discriminator is not needed, and the resulting filter structure can be significantly simplified.
entries.comment: 15 pages, 17 figures. The paper is accepted for publication in the journal "Radiotechnika" (Radio engineering)

entries.title: Target Selection with a Disappearing-Stimulus Mixed-Reality P300 Interface: Feasibility and Object-Distinguishable Versus Uniform Cues
entries.abstract: Mixed-reality (MR) P300 interfaces can register selectable destinations, such as wheelchair goals, directly in the user's surroundings. When the cues disappear between flashes, however, the user must retain an intended target that is no longer visible. We tested whether such an interface supports target selection and whether giving each cue a stable colour-shape identity improves it compared with visually uniform spheres. Six healthy adults completed four trials in each cue condition of a 5x5 row/column task on a head-mounted MR display, with EEG from Fz, Cz, and Pz. Shrinkage linear discriminant analysis was evaluated with nested validation in which complete trials were held out from class balancing, hyperparameter selection, and fitting. Both conditions evoked a parietal target-related positivity. The decoded cell was correct in 18 of 48 held-out trials, against 1.9 expected by chance (binomial p < 1e-12), and in three participants individually. Cue format made no detectable difference: complete-target accuracy was 9/24 in both conditions (paired difference 0.0 percentage points, 95% CI [-37, 37]), and held-out AUC was 0.609 for spheres and 0.585 for object cues. Disappearing-stimulus MR P300 selection is therefore feasible under strict trial-level evaluation, but the benefit of object identity, if any, is too small to resolve in a pilot of this size.
entries.comment: 5 pages, 2 figures, 1 table

entries.title: MusicFlux: Flexible Conditioning for Text-Guided Music Generation and Editing
entries.abstract: Music editing transforms existing recordings while preserving their original attributes. Recent approaches adapt pretrained text-to-music models for tasks like inpainting, event insertion, or restoration by conditioning them with context audio. It was recently proposed for image editing to unify generation and editing by treating the source image as in-context information. However, applying this directly to music is computationally expensive due to long audio sequences. In this work, we develop MusicFlux, a text-guided music editor built on an efficient pretrained flow-matching text-to-audio model. We introduce two conditioning approaches that trade off editing performance and computational efficiency. Experiments show that both are competitive with strong baselines, with one achieving better editing quality and the other preserving the original sequence length and substantially improving computational efficiency.
authors: Leonardo Boulitreau de Menezes Martins Marques
entries.comment: Submitted to ICASSP 2027

entries.title: A Faster and Efficient Indoor User Localization Using Bistatic MIMO Radar
entries.abstract: Indoor user localization is essential for applications such as asset tracking, robotic navigation, and smart-building automation where satellite-based positioning is unavailable. Bistatic MIMO radar exploits bistatic range measurements and geometric diversity from distributed antennas, but low-SNR conditions make the resulting estimation ill-conditioned. We formulate indoor localization as a Tikhonov-regularized nonlinear least-squares problem and solve it with a damped Gauss-Newton (DGN) algorithm, in which each iteration reduces to a closed-form 3x3 linear solve followed by an Armijo backtracking line search. Simulations show accuracy on par with, and runtime far faster than, an SDP-based benchmark.
entries.comment: 6 pages, 5 figures

entries.title: RaGCD: Reliability-Aware 2D-3D Multimodal Generalized Category Discovery
entries.abstract: Generalized Category Discovery (GCD) aims to recognize known categories while discovering novel ones from partially labeled data. Existing GCD studies primarily focus on unimodal observations or image-text interactions, leaving the complementarity between visual appearance and explicit 3D geometry underexplored. To exploit complementary visual appearance and spatial geometry, we investigate GCD with paired images and point clouds. However, the relative reliability of these modalities varies across samples, so unreliable evidence can compromise both multimodal fusion and cross-modal knowledge transfer. This challenge is particularly pronounced for novel categories, where labeled supervision is unavailable. To address it, we propose RaGCD, a reliability-aware framework for 2D-3D multimodal GCD. Specifically, Reliability-aware Modality Allocation (RMA) combines prediction-derived reliability cues with modality-specific features to adaptively allocate image and point-cloud contributions at the channel level. Reliability-conditioned Alignment (RCA) further reweights feature-level and prediction-level alignment and selects reliable observations for prototype-level alignment, regulating cross-modal interaction according to sample reliability. Extensive experiments on ModelNet40, Washington RGB-D, and ShapeNet-ViPC demonstrate that RaGCD outperforms the compared methods in overall and novel-category clustering accuracy. Ablation studies support the complementary roles of RMA and RCA, while controlled corruption experiments show that modality allocation shifts toward the less corrupted modality. These results support the effectiveness of reliability-aware interaction for category discovery from paired appearance and geometry.

entries.title: Mixed Signals: Weight-Space Programming for EEG and ECG
entries.abstract: Weight-space programming allows language models to read a trained neural network's weights and edit them. This opens the door to “training” by reasoning rather than through gradient descent. Prior work has demonstrated its functionality and promise for game-playing networks and fixing specific failures in language models, even extending to diffusion models. In this work, we present its applicability to models trained on biosignal data, specifically EEG and ECG data. We show that frontier models are not only able to debug specific faults planted in biosignal-based models without being told what these faults are, but are even capable of writing all the weights of a network from scratch, given only the architecture, the task, and a minimal set of training subjects. In particular, in one set of experiments, a language model was able to match standard gradient-descent training using 6× fewer training subjects, through reasoning alone and without any gradient descent step. Networks written by Claude Opus 5.5 also scored higher than classic hand-crafted EEG pipelines (alpha band power, and common spatial patterns with linear discriminant analysis) when built from the same 5 subjects. We also highlight some of the limitations, which include the inability of language models to improve already well-trained classification models, and their incapacity to reliably recognize, from the weights alone, the task a network was trained on. Overall, our results indicate that weight-space programming can be useful for small networks, such as those deployed on edge devices and wearables, but the concept still requires further investigation before it can be used in practice.
entries.comment: 9 pages, 7 figures, 5 tables. Project website: https://daravaram.github.io/BioWSP

entries.title: Multi-Step Underwater Acoustic Channel Prediction via Dual-Domain Structure Preservation and Pretrained Transformer
entries.abstract: Accurate future channel state information (CSI) is essential for underwater acoustic (UWA) communication because delays associated with signal propagation, feedback, scheduling, and transceiver reconfiguration can render currently available CSI outdated. However, most existing predictors estimate only the next channel state and obtain multi-step forecasts through recursive rollout, which causes prediction errors to accumulate as the multipath structure evolves. The scarcity of sea-trial measurements further limits reliable model training. To address these challenges, we propose LLM4UACP, a dual-domain, structure-preserving framework that adapts a pretrained Transformer for few-shot multi-step UWA channel prediction. LLM4UACP extracts complementary features from the channel impulse response (CIR) and channel frequency response (CFR), aligns them through Fourier-consistent fusion, and encodes the fused representation as delay-time tokens. A pretrained Transformer with a frozen backbone is adapted through Butterfly Orthogonal Fine-tuning to jointly predict multiple future CIRs in a single forward pass, thereby avoiding the error accumulation associated with recursive prediction. Experiments on the measured SO-06 and SO-07 channels show that LLM4UACP achieves normalized mean squared error (NMSE) values of 0.0411 and 0.0399, corresponding to reductions of 88.53% and 85.15%, respectively, relative to the most recent baseline. With only 0.11M trainable parameters, LLM4UACP maintains robust performance across varying prediction horizons and observation-window lengths, limited-data settings, and cross-dataset transfer scenarios.

entries.title: Residual-Closed-Loop SAGE-Brent Estimation for Unknown-Order Wideband Underwater Acoustic Channels
entries.abstract: Grid mismatch in wideband channel estimation leaves structured cancellation residuals after strong-path subtraction. These residuals generate spurious correlation peaks or mask weak arrivals, turning continuous parameter errors into path-count errors. We propose RC-SAGE-Brent, a residual-closed-loop estimator that jointly refines continuous delay-scale parameters and corrects the unknown-order path set. Within each feedback cycle, ambiguity-constrained alternating Brent searches suppress strong-path cancellation residuals. Candidate validation, resolution-constrained pruning, and full-domain residual redetection then revise the active path set. For linear frequency modulation (LFM) probes, an observable signal-to-residual ratio adaptively scales the model-order penalty to mitigate overestimation caused by delay-scale coupling. Theoretical analysis links off-grid parameter errors to local cancellation-residual curvature and weak-path detectability. Factorial ablations, paired comparisons against standard sparse and off-grid estimators, and measured channel replay demonstrate improved path-set recovery and waveform reconstruction while delineating the operational boundaries of the method.
entries.comment: 31 pages, 14 figures, 9 tables. Includes supplementary materials (Tables S1-S5)

entries.title: Toward Pseudorange-Based PNT with Starlink: A Mock Fused LEO GNSS Implementation
entries.abstract: We present experimental results from Starlink for pseudorange-based positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT), emulating a system that fuses a primary communications mission with a secondary low-Earth orbit (LEO) PNT mission. Legacy global navigation satellite system (GNSS) constellations faceinherent vulnerabilities and signal limitations, prompting growing interest in broadband LEO constellations—such as SpaceX's Starlink—for resilient PNT. However, opportunistic use of stand-alone Starlink signals fails to achieve GNSS-competitive accuracy due to frame timing irregularities and reliance on uncorrected poor-quality publicly available ephemeris data. To overcome these limitations, we present a mock implementation of a fused LEO GNSS architecture. Our method extracts time-of-arrival observables from live Starlink Ku-band downlinks and pairs them with high-fidelity, beam-specific orbit and clock models distributed as if provided natively by the constellation operator. In a field campaign, and despite constraints imposed by consumer-grade receiver hardware, the method yields 95% error bounds of 2.33 m horizontally (semi-major axis), 3.37 m vertically, and 11.19 ns in timing, with the actual solution errors falling well within these bounds.

entries.title: MouldIt: Data Efficiency of Multi-Task Temporal Representation Learning in Injection Moulding
entries.abstract: Smart industrial solutions that can address multiple tasks require models that understand the underlying processes. We examine representation learning for modeling the injection moulding process as an example of such solutions. We consider its data efficiency and multi-modal benefit compared to classical machine learning alternatives. To this end, we synthesize a process-informed dataset based on a real reference cycle of an Erlanger Träger part. We then introduce MouldIt, a temporal convolution and attention based variational autoencoder that reconstructs in-mould signals, while classifying parts as acceptable or as one of our synthetic failure modes. We evaluate MouldIt on two tasks, known-class classification and unknown-class detection, across nine dataset sizes in single-modal and multi-modal settings. We compare it with an accept-all baseline and the classical methods k-nearest neighbors, logistic regression, random forests, and principal component analysis, which we adapt to support both tasks. MouldIt outperforms classical methods across both tasks from 4000 cycles in the single-modal setting and from 2000 cycles in the multi-modal setting. It achieves part sorting losses of 6.0 ± 0.7% and 1.0 ± 0.3% in the single-modal and multi-modal settings respectively, ranking first across all baselines and a combination of principal component analysis and random forests.
entries.comment: 14 pages, 10 figures, 4 tables

entries.title: Stability Analysis of Single- and Multi-Snapshot ESPRIT
entries.abstract: Spectral estimation seeks to recover unknown frequencies from T snapshots, each consisting of Ω+1 noisy Fourier measurements. Super-resolution refers to the recovery of frequencies whose minimum separation Δ is smaller than 1/Ω. We establish state-of-the-art stability bounds for single- and multi-snapshot ESPRIT when the frequencies form well-separated clumps, with the largest clump containing n* frequencies. In particular, for single-snapshot ESPRIT, our error bound scales as O(Ω⁻¹SRF^(2n^*-2)·Noise), where SRF:=(ΩΔ)⁻¹ denotes the super-resolution factor, provided that the noise level satisfies Noise(ΩΔ)^(2n^*-2). In comparison with the minimax bounds [arXiv:1904.09186] and the computational resolution limits [arXiv:2003.02917, arXiv:2211.15208], our result shows that single-snapshot ESPRIT achieves the optimal stability scaling in the super-resolution regime. For multi-snapshot ESPRIT, we establish error bounds under both deterministic noise and Gaussian white noise, attaining the best-known SRF dependence under weaker conditions. Numerical experiments corroborate the theoretical error bounds.

entries.title: Joint Air Corridor and BS Coverage Planning for Large-Scale High-Density Low-Altitude Aerial Networks via Channel Knowledge Maps
entries.abstract: This paper studies the joint air corridor and base station (BS) coverage planning problem for high-density low-altitude aerial networks supported by terrestrial cellular infrastructures. In the considered system, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) operate within a structured air corridor planned over a grid-based airspace, and each BS serves selected corridor grid cells by sharing its communication resources among all UAVs therein. Each BS's traffic load depends on both the number of covered corridor cells and the UAV density, thereby affecting the communication rate available to each UAV. We exploit the channel knowledge map (CKM) to characterize the channel gains between BSs and candidate airspace cells and evaluate desired signals and inter-cell interference for environment-aware offline planning. Based on CKM, we jointly optimize the corridor layout and BS coverage to minimize a weighted objective balancing corridor length and the supportable average UAV density along the entire corridor, subject to minimum communication rate requirements for all UAVs along the air corridor. The joint design is formulated as a mixed-integer linear program (MILP), which can be optimally solved using off-the-shelf solvers. For large maps, we develop a scalable suboptimal algorithm based on Lagrangian relaxation and A* search. Specifically, we incorporate BS resource constraints into A* corridor search via Lagrangian relaxation, and then jointly optimize BS coverage and UAV density along the generated corridors under the original rate constraints. Numerical results demonstrate the benefits of the proposed joint design in supporting high-density UAV operations and show that the proposed algorithm obtains high-quality solutions with substantially reduced computation time.

entries.title: Distribution Shift Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery using Machine Learning Models
entries.abstract: Remote sensing imagery acquired by Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) supports wide range of applications; however, deploying machine learning (ML) models on resource-constrained aerial platforms introduces challenges beyond predictive accuracy, particularly when deployment data differ from the distributions observed during training. Such shifts are common in remote sensing due to geographic, sensor, seasonal, and other visual variations. A practical solution is to equip deployed models with mechanisms that detect emerging distribution shifts and support subsequent responsive actions. This paper presents an empirical case study of three open-source detection tools: (i) Alibi-Detect; (ii) NannyML; and (iii) PyTorch-OOD. Using cross-dataset remote-sensing shifts, we evaluate both detection effectiveness and computational latency of these tools. Our results reveal differences in detection behavior and processing cost across methods and implementations, highlighting trade-offs between detection capability and response-time. These findings motivate further work toward lightweight, and latency-aware monitoring mechanisms for resource-constrained systems.
entries.comment: Accepted as a short paper at the 4th Workshop on Computer Vision for Earth Observation (CV4EO), held in conjunction with WACV 2027

entries.title: Design and Over-the-Air Evaluation of a Digital Twin-Driven Site-Specific Neural Receiver for 5G NR on NVIDIA DGX Spark
entries.abstract: We design and evaluate a site-specific neural receiver for the 5G New Radio (NR) uplink. A corridor digital twin built from a radar scan and refined manually provides 28,671 ray-traced channel records for training an eight-round convolutional graph neural network with pilot-aware inputs and auxiliary channel supervision. The GPU on NVIDIA DGX Spark evaluates time–frequency convolutions in parallel across the received grid to accelerate inference. The receiver uses the standard NR uplink waveform and reference signals and feeds soft bits to the existing transport-block decoder. In over-the-air tests with NI USRP B210 radios under common radio settings, the site-trained receiver achieves the highest mean uplink rate at all five positions. At a non-line-of-sight corner, it reaches 16.2 Mb/s, compared with 4.1 Mb/s for the conventional receiver and 2.4 Mb/s for the 3GPP-trained neural receiver. These results demonstrate the feasibility of integrating neural reception into the 5G NR physical layer and show its potential for AI-RAN deployments.

entries.title: ARIA: An AI-Powered Radio-Channel Inference and Analysis Pipeline
entries.abstract: Statistical channel models play a key role in the design and standardization of next-generation wireless systems. The models substitute for costly and time-consuming field measurements when fitted distributions accurately reproduce the measured channel impulse responses. Future wireless systems will operate in global spectrum allocations from 1 to 150 GHz. Over the full span, analytically chosen distribution families fitted to scarce measurement data fail to deliver the required accuracy. Generative AI models instead learn each distribution from the radio-propagation data itself, adapt to the measured structure at every frequency, and scale across the entire band. We present ARIA, an AI-powered Radio-channel Inference and Analysis pipeline that learns each channel-parameter distribution from the measurements. The pipeline extracts power-delay profiles and recovers the channel parameters with time-cluster spatial-lobe (TCSL) analysis. Three neural density estimators, namely mixture density networks, neural spline flows (NSF), and denoising diffusion implicit models, learn each parameter's distribution. A composite rank across goodness-of-fit metrics with Friedman-Nemenyi testing identifies the best estimator, and a maximum-likelihood step anchored to the measured samples converts its density into closed-form parametric families. We instantiate ARIA on the NYU WIRELESS 16.95 GHz InH campaign and find that NSF outperforms the other estimators on every metric. We also show that a conditional NSF with feature-wise linear modulation, trained jointly on the 6.75 and 16.95 GHz measurements, improves over single-frequency training. We feed the fitted distributions into the NYUSIM simulator and reproduce the measured omnidirectional RMS delay spread medians within 2 ns, the per-lobe azimuth and zenith spread medians within 1 degree, and the omnidirectional zenith spread medians within 0.5 degrees.
entries.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication

entries.title: Thickness-Field-Excited Bimorph Piezoelectric Micromachined Ultrasonic Transducer in Submicrometer Thin-Film Lithium Niobate
entries.abstract: This work presents the first demonstration of a submicrometer-thick thickness-field-excited (TFE) lithium niobate (LN) flexural-mode piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducer (PMUT). A 670-nm-thick bilayer periodically poled piezoelectric film (P3F) 128Y LN is used to demonstrate a suspended membrane with an area of 0.25 mm², achieving a low resonance frequency of 33.4 kHz for airborne transduction. Its electrical measurements reveal an extracted effective electromechanical coupling efficiency (k_eff²) of 3% and a moderate static capacitance C₀ of 17 pF. Meanwhile, mechanical measurements using a laser Doppler vibrometer (LDV) yield a high quasi-static peak out-of-plane displacement (ξ_static) of 145 nm/V and a high corresponding open-circuit sensitivity (S_OC) of 1.4 mV/Pa in the audio band. The fabricated device is compared with state-of-the-art (SoA) airborne piezoelectric transducers with sub-100-kHz resonance frequencies, underscoring the potential of the TFE P3F LN transducer platform by simultaneously demonstrating strong actuation capability while featuring high sensitivity.
entries.comment: 8 pages, 11 figures

entries.title: STAR: Semantic-Criticality Tiered Allocation of Radio Resources via Zero-Shot Learning
entries.abstract: In remote inference, edge devices transmit high-resolution images over wireless links to a receiver, where an artificial intelligence (AI) model answers task-specific questions about these images to enable reliable decisions. These answers are often determined by a small set of task-causal pixels, such as those of text, whose corruption changes the answer, so these pixels must be delivered with high fidelity. Conventional transmission protects every pixel equally, so it either consumes many resource elements (REs) or corrupts these regions at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). To overcome these limitations, in this paper, a zero-shot, domain-agnostic framework, termed semantic-criticality tiered allocation of resources (STAR), is proposed. In particular, a per-pixel semantic-criticality indicator (SCI) is derived from the attention of a frozen vision-language model, so new tasks and domains are handled by changing only the prompt, without retraining. The resulting task causality-aware resource allocation problem over protection tiers is solved exactly by a threshold rule on the SCI, realized by a coded tier for the task-causal pixels and an uncoded, downsampled base layer for the full image. Simulations over a 5G New Radio link demonstrate that STAR attains a semantic accuracy of at least 0.98 for E_s/N₀ ≥-4 dB and, at comparable semantic reliability, reduces the REs of robust coded transmission by 59.5% and 91.5% on factory- and vehicle-monitoring datasets, respectively, the latter without any change to the models. Although a deep joint source-channel coding baseline uses fewer REs at comparable semantic accuracy, it must be retrained with labeled data for every new task or domain.
entries.comment: 6 pages, 9 figures, 1 table. Submitted to IEEE ICC 2027

entries.title: Coexistence of Direct-to-Device (D2D) Satellite Systems with 5G/6G Terrestrial Networks: Cross-Border Aggregate Interference Analysis in Saudi Arabia
entries.abstract: Direct-to-device (D2D) satellite systems, particularly those based on 3GPP-compliant non-terrestrial networks (NTN), deliver connectivity to standard mobile phones and IoT devices using terrestrial International Mobile Telecommunications (IMT) spectrum. This raises the risk of harmful cross-border interference into incumbent terrestrial IMT networks, an issue considered under Agenda Item 1.13 of the ITU World Radiocommunication Conference 2027 (WRC-27). This paper presents an ITU-R-compliant assessment of aggregate downlink interference from two hypothetical D2D systems operating in Jordan and Iraq into terrestrial IMT user equipment (UE) in Saudi Arabia, operating in the 698-960 MHz band. Unlike prior studies that evaluate a few test points near a simplified ideal tri-border intersection, we distribute multiple victim UEs along realistic national borders within various strips at a distance of 0-40 km from the borders. We compare two satellite selection strategies: highest-elevation and random strategies. The CDF of the interference-to-noise ratio (I/N) together with the intra-system and inter-system aggregation factors are analyzed. Results show that the protection criterion is exceeded up to 88% of the time, requiring up to 27 dB of additional isolation, so coexistence is infeasible without interference mitigation. In general, random selection produces higher interference because low-elevation beams place victims closer to boresight. Two mitigation techniques are then evaluated. A border isolation zone of one cell diameter yields only a moderate improvement under both strategies, whereas a narrow-beam, deep-null phased-array pattern lowers the exceedance to about 40% irrespective of strategy, providing an important input for spectrum regulatory considerations.

entries.title: WaveGen: Truly End-to-End Waveform Generation via Internal Spectral Trajectory Learning
entries.abstract: This work proposes WaveGen, a fully end-to-end diffusion-based text-to-waveform framework based on Spectral Forcing, which jointly learns an internal spectral trajectory and the target waveform trajectory within a single model, enabling direct end-to-end text-to-waveform generation. Unlike recent TTS pipelines, WaveGen does not rely on separately trained or externally decoded intermediate representations, such as neural audio codecs, Mel-spectrogram vocoders, or VAE-based latent models. In addition, WaveGen performs internal text-speech alignment within a single model, eliminating the need for external alignment modules such as duration predictors. To preserve a truly end-to-end formulation, our framework further avoids dependence on self-supervised representations, such as BERT-based text embeddings and Wav2Vec 2.0-based semantic representations, as well as semantic distillation methods for training optimization. To achieve this, we carefully design Spectral Forcing, a model architecture with disentangled diffusion heads, and a training objective based on a multi-scale spectral v-loss. We further validate the scalability of end-to-end TTS models by scaling the model size from 0.1B to 0.6B parameters. Using a single architecture, open-source data, and one-stage training, without external modules such as duration predictor or REPA, WaveGen demonstrates fully end-to-end waveform generation achieving state-of-the-art performance on the Emilia training dataset. In particular, WaveGen achieves a WER of 1.47 and a SIM of 0.75 on the Seed-en benchmark. Source code and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/sh-lee-prml/WaveGen
entries.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026

entries.title: Reference-Dependent Utility Optimization for Goal-Oriented Communication Systems
entries.abstract: Traditional communication resource allocation optimizes operational metrics such as rate, latency, energy efficiency, and reliability. Motivated by goal-oriented semantic communication, we develop a generalized allocation framework that transforms operational rewards through reference-dependent user utilities and evaluates them via expected utility, cumulative prospect theory (CPT), or related decision criteria. The formulation separates operational rewards, user-side valuations, and system-level decision criteria under uncertainty. We characterize utilities incorporating QoS/service reference levels, deficit sensitivity, post-reference saturation, and loss aversion. Weighted sum-reward maximization, proportional fairness, α-fairness, and stochastic expected utility maximization emerge as exact special cases, while soft QoS-aware allocation follows from a deficit-penalty generalization. For deterministic orthogonal systems, we derive utility-weighted marginal-reward KKT conditions characterizing global optimality under concave composite objectives. For nonorthogonal and stochastic systems, we develop successive convex approximation (SCA) algorithms and establish stationary-point guarantees under explicit smooth and composite nonsmooth assumptions, including a CPT branch-stationarity result under eventual nondegenerate ordering identification. For globally solved penalized problems, we derive an O(1/λ) bound on excess aggregate soft-QoS deficit, and on the deficit itself whenever a QoS-feasible allocation exists. Additionally, we establish an O(1/ε²) outer iteration bound for the smooth fixed-step SCA best-response residual. Numerical examples demonstrate how reference points, marginal utility slopes, channel quality, and resource budgets influence active users and allocation policies.
entries.comment: This paper has been submitted for publication

entries.title: Grid Design for Near-Field Channel Estimation with Uniform Linear Arrays
entries.abstract: This paper develops deterministic grids for line-of-sight near-field channel estimation with uniform linear arrays (ULAs) and hybrid receivers. A normalized channel approximation squared error (NCASE) criterion leads to geometric covering problems under a constant-amplitude parabolic model and an elliptical approximation of the correlation regions. For a horizontal ULA, transformation and scaling yield a disk-covering problem, addressed by adapting a hexagonal lattice to the mapped ground-plane region. For a vertical ULA, a reciprocal-distance interval cover is solved optimally by a farthest-reaching greedy procedure. Numerical evaluation with exact spherical-wave channels yields empirical maximum approximation errors close to the target and improved P-SOMP estimation relative to the tested polar-domain grids of comparable size.

entries.title: Neural Multipath Fields for 6G FR3 Digital Twins: Latent Adaptation from Sparse Data
entries.abstract: Wireless digital twins are essential for environment-aware 6G communications, motivating the investigation of frequency range 3 (FR3), an emerging mid-band regime offering a promising balance between bandwidth and propagation characteristics. Neural Radio Frequency (RF) fields provide continuous surrogates for site-specific radio propagation, but adapting a scene-specific field to a new environment can require substantial measurements and retraining. To this end, we propose the Latent-Adaptive Neural Multipath Field (LANMF), a scene-conditioned FR3 model that predicts path-resolved delays, complex channel impulse response (CIR) coefficients, and arrival and departure directions from transmitter-receiver coordinates. LANMF learns shared propagation representations across source environments and adapts to unseen scenes by optimizing only a 16-dimensional scene latent. Evaluated on six ray-traced indoor scenes at 7.5 GHz, latent-only adaptation yields improvements in prediction with just 5-10 target links (0.42-0.83% of available links). Compared with full-network fine-tuning, it updates only 16 persistent target parameters, reducing adaptation time by 28-30% and incremental peak GPU memory by 82-85%. While the proposed solution supports various wireless applications, we demonstrate its utility through beam-candidate reduction using a 64-beam codebook, retaining measurement-based final beam selection.

entries.title: VNA-Only Calibration of Waveguide Thermistor Mounts with Self-Consistent Determination of the Thermistor-Port Impedance
entries.abstract: A method is presented for determining the calibration factor and the effective efficiency of waveguide thermistor mounts from vector-network-analyzer reflection data alone, without a microcalorimeter, extending the three reflection-coefficient method of the coaxial case. In waveguide the thermistor is coupled to the line through a matching structure and the reference impedance of the thermistor port, Z₀, is not known a priori; it is inferred through a power-consistency relation between pairs of states, under the convention that it is real. The method reproduces the factory certificates (U = 2%) of four K486A mounts within 1.0% rms and the PTB-traceable values (U = 0.85 to 0.98%) of a fifth within 0.34% rms; its expanded measurement uncertainty is 0.5 to 1.16% (k = 2) for the best specimen and below 2% for the five. A mount with its waveguide-to-coaxial adapter is calibrated directly, without characterizing the adapter, from the model factor of the mount and the geometric factor measured through the adapter. The scattering matrix implied by the solution is not passive; a minimum-norm correction of the thermistor impedances along the two directions invisible to the calibration factor - the ratios of the efficiencies of the three states - brings it to the floor of passivity, where the efficiency depends on the load only through its mismatch factor, leaves the result unchanged, and gives the sensitivity of the efficiency to the bias resistance in closed form: below 4×10⁻⁵ Ω⁻¹ in band mean, proportional to the mismatch of the operating state and to the loss of the mount.
entries.comment: 60 pages, 21 figures. Submitted to Metrologia (IOP Publishing / BIPM), November 2026

entries.title: Robust Beamforming and Antenna Position Optimization for Movable Antenna-Assisted Covert Communications
entries.abstract: In this paper, we study a movable antenna (MA)-enhanced covert communication system, where a legitimate transmitter (Alice) serves multiple legitimate users in the presence of multiple non-colluding Willies that attempt to detect the covert transmission from Alice. To ensure data covertness with imperfect knowledge of the Willies' channel state information (CSI), we develop a robust covert transmission framework with a norm-bounded CSI error model. In particular, we aim to jointly optimize the transmit beamforming vectors, artificial noise (AN) covariance matrix, and MA positions to maximize the weighted minimum signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) among all legitimate users subject to worst-case covertness constraints. To tackle this challenging problem, we develop a block coordinate descent (BCD)-based optimization framework, incorporating the S-procedure, semidefinite relaxation (SDR), bisection search, and successive convex approximation (SCA). Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed algorithm in improving the performance of MA-enhanced covert communication systems.

entries.title: A Scale-Space Theory of Memory
entries.abstract: Scale-space theory has emerged as a central attempt to restrict the general theory of signal processing with geometric constraints inspired from the animal world. In the mathematical language of operator theory, scale-space theory restricts the Toeplitz operator. The present paper investigates scale-space theory for memory systems. We investigate how scale space theory restricts a memory system encoding past information, that is, restricts the Hankel operator. Our main result is to establish a close correspondence between scale-space theory and the long-studied relaxation property.

entries.title: Movable Antenna-Assisted Covert Communications: Robust Beamforming and Antenna Position Optimization
entries.abstract: In this paper, we study a movable antenna (MA)-enhanced covert communication system, where a legitimate transmitter (named Alice) serves multiple legitimate users in the presence of multiple aerial wardens that attempt to detect the transmission from Alice. To ensure data covertness with imperfect knowledge of warden channel state information (CSI), we develop a unified robust covert transmission framework that incorporates bounded and statistical CSI error models. In particular, we aim to jointly optimize the transmit beamforming, the artificial noise (AN) covariance matrix, and MA positions at Alice to maximize the minimum weighted signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) among the legitimate users subject to data covertness constraints. The resulting optimization problem is intractable to solve optimally due to the strong coupling among the optimization variables and the random channel uncertainty. To deal with this issue, we propose a block coordinate descent (BCD)-based algorithm. Specifically, for the norm-bounded CSI error model, we first employ the S-procedure to convert the covertness constraints into a sequence of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Then, a successive convex approximation (SCA) procedure incorporating semidefinite relaxation (SDR) and bisection search techniques is proposed to solve the resulting problem. For the statistical CSI error model, the Bernstein-type inequality is employed to derive deterministic approximations of the probabilistic constraint in terms of LMIs and second-order cone (SOC) constraints that can be efficiently tackled. Numerical results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed algorithm in improving the performance of MA-enhanced covert communication systems.

entries.title: Mitigating the BICM Loss in MIMO Receivers with Correlation-Informed Logits
entries.abstract: Bit-interleaved coded modulation (BICM) is widely used in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) wireless systems. However, separating MIMO data detection from channel decoding and only exchanging per-bit soft information discards correlation information among the bits within each transmit vector. We show that the resulting information loss limits the performance of practical one-shot receivers. Even though iterative detection and decoding (IDD) can recover most of this loss, IDD significantly increases receiver complexity and latency. In order to reduce this loss, we propose COrrelation-Informed Logits (COIL), a soft-output format that combines per-bit soft information with pairwise coupling logits for correlated bits. We show how to incorporate these coupling logits into a conventional belief-propagation-based channel decoder, which enables correlation-aware decoding in a one-shot receiver without IDD. We evaluate COIL in a MIMO-BICM system with a conventional low-density parity-check code. For a 4x4 MIMO orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) system, a one-shot linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE) receiver with COIL outperforms a conventional one-shot unbiased LMMSE receiver by 1.3dB and operates within 0.8dB of four-iteration IDD, while requiring only a single pass through the data detector.
entries.comment: Submitted to a journal

entries.title: Spectral-Domain Information Geometry of Stationary Covariance Models: Gaussian and Elliptical Extensions
entries.abstract: This paper develops an information-geometric framework for stationary covariance structures. We begin with the infinite-dimensional setting, where stationary covariance structures can be characterized without finite-window boundary effects. By formulating the covariance structure as a bilinear form on a suitable class of test functions, we establish its spectral representation and show how finite-dimensional Toeplitz covariance matrices arise as restrictions to nested observation subspaces. For zero-mean proper complex Gaussian wide-sense stationary (WSS) processes, we show that the normalized finite-dimensional Fisher information converges to a spectral-domain metric. In logarithmic spectral coordinates, this metric becomes the standard L² inner product, yielding an explicit Fisher–Rao distance that is also recovered as the asymptotic normalized affine-invariant Riemannian distance between Toeplitz covariance matrices. We then extend the framework to elliptical observation models by separating global covariance scale from shape. The shape Fisher information is orthogonal to radial nuisance directions and is characterized by a dimension- and radial-model-dependent coefficient. We derive a condition under which this coefficient converges to its Gaussian value as the observation dimension tends to infinity. The resulting limiting spectral-shape geometry is the centered L² geometry of log-spectra and is invariant to positive rescaling. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical convergence results and the recovery of the Gaussian shape coefficient.
entries.comment: 26 pages, 7 figures

entries.title: Joint Power and Adaptive-Constellation Optimization for OFDM-ISAC Systems
entries.abstract: Next-generation wireless systems are expected to support integrated sensing and communications (ISAC). However, sensing imposes different requirements on the power allocation (PA) and the modulation format than communications, leading to a fundamental trade-off in frequency-selective channels. In this paper, we jointly optimize the PA and modulation format for orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM)-based ISAC systems, considering both target detection and tracking. We first derive an upper bound on the mutual information to predict the communication performance for power-constellation allocation. We then use an autoencoder (AE) to learn a family of finite constellations that realizes the allocation under different sensing constraints without retraining. The results show that tracking alleviates the sensing & communications (S&C) tradeoff compared with initial detection, and that the PA and the modulation dominate the S&C trade-off at low and high signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), respectively. At intermediate SNR, the proposed joint optimization significantly outperforms individual optimizations, while the pretrained adaptive constellation family almost fully realizes the predicted allocation gains.
entries.comment: Accepted at 1st IEEE Conference on Integrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC), Lisbon, Portugal, Nov. 2026

entries.title: Prospective Importance-based Cognitive Pilot Design for Semantic Sensing in ISAC Systems
entries.abstract: Semantic sensing enables integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems to acquire environmental information relevant to downstream tasks. However, existing pilot design methods either rely on static pilot configurations or learn end-to-end pilot selection policies, without explicitly evaluating the semantic contribution of candidate pilot locations. In this work, we propose a cognitive semantic sensing framework for human activity recognition in orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM)-ISAC systems. Rather than directly learning a high-dimensional mapping from observations to pilot locations, we introduce a semantic importance weight (SIW) to measure the semantic contribution of each candidate pilot location. Leveraging the information bottleneck (IB) principle and the mutual information-minimum mean-square error (I-MMSE) relationship, SIW assigns high values to future time-frequency (TF) channel coefficients that are both difficult to infer from the preceding observations and valuable for downstream inference. To efficiently obtain the SIW, we further develop a conditional diffusion model that predicts the corresponding uncertainty through denoising covariance estimation. Experiments on a real-world Wi-Fi sensing dataset show that the proposed method consistently outperforms baselines across different signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) and pilot budgets.
entries.comment: The paper has been submitted to the 2027 WCNC conference

entries.title: Split-Ring Couplers for On-Skin Wi-Fi Communication via an SSPP Waveguide Textile
entries.abstract: Textile spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) waveguides offer guided on-body links, but their body-facing ground conductors obstruct coupling from on-skin wireless nodes. This letter presents a split-ring coupling interface using local ground recesses at the textile terminations, without patterned garment-side launchers. The capacitively loaded rings are supported by polydimethylsiloxane carriers with a thickness of 2 mm. An image-current model and full-wave simulations examine the effect of backing-ground spacing and determine the recess geometry. For a 450 mm textile waveguide on a water-filled body phantom, the measured S₂₁ at 2.45 GHz was -18.8 dB, versus -60.9 dB without the textile. A 625-position scan showed a maximum 5.1 dB reduction relative to the nominal position within the measured joint ±5 mm placement region. A separate two-node IEEE 802.11n test demonstrated a 65 Mb/s physical-layer (PHY) rate with zero packet errors among 300 frames at -20 dBm transmit power through the coupler link. These results establish high-rate, placement-tolerant on-skin Wi-Fi communication through an SSPP waveguide textile.
entries.comment: 4 pages, 6 figures

entries.title: MambaPD: Bidirectional Selective State Space Model for Parkinson's Disease Detection from Resting-State EEG
entries.abstract: Typical diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (PD) occurs only after significant dopaminergic loss, while resting-state EEG abnormalities like alpha slowing and reduced coherence occur earlier. While many published EEG-based PD detectors claim accuracy greater than 95%, many use epoch-level splits which leak subject identity. I introduce MambaPD, a bidirectional selective state space model for resting-state EEG-based PD detection, blending the channel mixing, patch tokenization and bidirectional Mamba encoder. It is compared with four baselines (TCN, BiLSTM with attention, EEGNet and a patch Transformer) in two public datasets (UNM, SanDiego) using subject-independent 5-fold cross-validation (checkpoints were selected on the held-out fold, so absolute estimates are optimistic). On UNM the accuracy is between 0.67 and 0.71, and MambaPD (0.714) is not statistically distinguishable from the Transformer (0.715), and TCN (0.708), with the highest sensitivity (0.82), while the lowest specificity (0.52). For the smaller SanDiego cohort, accuracy is in the range of 0.60 to 0.70, with the highest scores (0.703) from TCN and the lowest (0.601) from EEGNet, while MambaPD scores 0.631, with the lowest specificity (0.46) among the five models. The differences among the models on UNM are minor compared to the differences among folds. I report the whole pipeline, per-fold results, and the shortcomings of the protocol.
entries.comment: 17 pages, 11 figures, 9 tables

entries.title: Near-Field Channel Estimation via Deep Unfolding for Extremely Large-Scale Antenna Arrays
entries.abstract: The Extremely Large-scale Antenna Array (ELAA) has been envisioned as a promising candidate to meet the ambitious demands of 6G. However, this evolution also brings about two primary limitations: high computational complexity caused by large-scale arrays and inherent operation in the near-field region. To address these issues, this work exploits the sparsity of near-field channels in the polar domain and formulates channel estimation as a compressed sensing (CS) problem, thereby enabling estimation with reduced pilot overhead. In particular, we propose a guideline to design a sparsifying codebook for the near-field channel, which is strictly based on a target coherence value. Building on this, we develop a deep unfolding architecture, derived from the iterative solver ISTA, with a hybrid loss, namely Hybrid LISTA. Numerical results demonstrate that our proposed codebook, with comparable complexity, still exhibits improved estimation performance and greater coverage in the near-field region. Moreover, our unfolded model with the hybrid loss consistently delivers better recovery performance over existing estimation schemes.
entries.comment: 6 pages, 7 figures, submitted to the 2026 International Conference on Advanced Technologies for Communications (ATC 2026), Best Paper Award

entries.title: Bistatic UAV-Based 3D SAR Imaging Using Integrated Sensing and Communications Transceivers
entries.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) frameworks enable autonomous systems to jointly perform radar sensing and wireless communication using common spectral and hardware resources. Prior art on ISAC-enabled UAV for SAR focused on monostatic configurations for two-dimensional target imaging. In this work, we propose a bistatic UAV tomographic SAR framework in which the IEEE 802.11ad waveform, RF hardware, and spectral resources are jointly utilized for communication and radar sensing for three-dimensional (3D) localization of complex targets. Specifically, we demonstrate how communication packets transmitted from a master ISAC transceiver UAV to a passive receiver UAV are exploited for timing and frequency synchronization, motion compensation, and 3D localization of targets, without requiring auxiliary infrastructure on the passive receiver for these tasks. We evaluate the proposed framework for localizing automotive targets over elevated terrain, with Monte Carlo simulations modeling synchronization and platform motion errors. The results demonstrate improved localization accuracy compared with conventional InSAR-based localization. The interplay between radar and communication performances are further evaluated using diverse modulation schemes.

entries.title: UltraVoxelGS: Voxel-First Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting for 3D Ultrasound Reconstruction
entries.abstract: We present UltraVoxelGS, a 3D ultrasound reconstruction method that achieves both fast reconstruction and physically faithful rendering for the first time, bringing live spatial feedback during 2D ultrasound scanning within reach. This is made possible by a feed-forward design that predicts a complete Gaussian scene representation from posed ultrasound images directly, entirely bypassing the per-scene optimization bottleneck that has confined prior methods to offline use. Realising such feed-forward prediction in this setting is non-trivial: unlike natural images, ultrasound slices share at most one-dimensional intersections and exhibit view-dependent appearance due to acoustic propagation and attenuation, violating the dense overlap and photometric consistency assumed by existing feed-forward Gaussian methods. Hence, to achieve fast reconstruction, we introduce a feed-forward voxel-to-Gaussian pass that decouples representation size from input count by lifting all posed slices into a fixed-size voxel support and predicting Gaussian parameters directly. For faithful rendering, we propose ultrasound-aware appearance rendering strategy factorize reflection from cumulative attenuation during training and exploit appearance continuity among spatially adjacent slices for efficient Render-time Appearance Adaptation. On both real-world and simulated datasets, UltraVoxelGS achieves best PSNR/SSIM compared with per-scene optimization baselines while reducing inference from 10-20 minutes to approximately 10 seconds (over 35 times faster) and scales to sequences exceeding 1,000 frames. Code is available at https://github.com/YuebyYue/UltraVoxelGS-camera-ready.

entries.title: Capture-Aware Predictive OFDM Reacquisition in Clock-Asynchronous Space-Air-Ground Networks
entries.abstract: Reliable orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) reacquisition must validate an intended burst and return its delay and carrier frequency offset (CFO) correc- tions within capture tolerances. In clock-asynchronous space- air-ground integrated networks (SAGINs), shared geometry and timing uncertainty couples distributed observations, while public- preamble replay creates competing peaks. We propose Capture- Aware Predictive Reacquisition (CAPR), a Bayesian receiver that models competition under both hypotheses and marginalizes unknown spatial interference covariance and target complex amplitude before shared-state fusion. CAPR maximizes posterior probability mass within the capture rectangle and constrains continuous L-BFGS-B refinement through a mass-loss budget. We derive closed-form predictive likelihood reductions, an exact finite-cell action optimizer, a conditional approximation regret bound, and finite-sample false-acceptance calibration. Across 150 primary scenarios and five seeds, CAPR achieves 83.8% strict capture at 4.68% realized false acceptance, improving over Gaussian joint-MAP by 12.5 percentage points overall and 54.2 points across all 32 replay scenarios. Diffuse multipath, degraded assistance, and indistinguishable sources delineate its operational boundaries.

entries.title: Distribution-Free Symmetry Detection in Multi-Reference Alignment at Low SNR
entries.abstract: Symmetry can reveal the structure of a signal, but detecting it becomes difficult when observations are noisy and randomly transformed. We study how to infer symmetry directly from multi-reference alignment data with additive isotropic Gaussian noise of known variance, without aligning the observations or knowing how the transformations were sampled. For cyclic symmetry, we identify a simple statistical signature that yields tests with exact finite-sample error guarantees. We demonstrate their performance even at very low signal-to-noise ratios. Dihedral symmetry presents a deeper challenge: we show that, for some signals, invariant moments below a sharp order threshold cannot distinguish reflectional from purely rotational symmetry. For generic signals, however, this distinction emerges much earlier. We use these insights to develop tests for dihedral symmetry with asymptotic error control under explicit nondegeneracy conditions. Together, the results clarify what we can learn about symmetry from noisy, unaligned data and suggest a path toward symmetry inference in cryo-EM.

entries.title: Integrating Deep PPG Representations and Digital Biomarkers for Aortic Stenosis Detection with Peri-TAVI Assessment
entries.abstract: Access to echocardiography is often limited, delaying recognition of progressive aortic stenosis (AS). A brief, low-cost physiological measurement obtained during routine care could help identify patients who may warrant earlier imaging. Here, we present PulseAS, integrating deep photoplethysmography (PPG) representations, waveform biomarkers and clinical information for high-grade AS screening. Three complementary analyses assessed (1) validation and transfer across cohorts differing in geography and ethnic composition, (2) score-based enrichment of AS and pre-transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) cases, and (3) preoperative and postoperative pulse changes. Using 15-s recordings, separate patient-level cross-validation in EDU (n = 1,209) and MIMIC-III (n = 2,970) yielded AUROCs of 0.818 (PulseAS-XGB) and 0.838 (PulseAS-L2), respectively. In external validation from MIMIC-III to EDU, PulseAS-XGB achieved an AUROC of 0.716, improving to 0.813 after local adaptation. The highest-scoring 10% captured 45.2% of all high-grade AS cases in EDU and 41.3% in MIMIC-III, and 56.9% of pre-TAVI cases in EDU. Notably, in the EDU TAVI subgroup, PPG waveforms showed earlier systolic peaks and narrower systolic contours following intervention. These findings support clinical-PPG risk stratification in new populations and warrant prospective evaluation of echocardiographic prioritisation.

entries.title: Joint LSFC and Nakagami-m Estimation From Downlink SINR in GZF-Precoded CF-mMIMO
entries.abstract: Accurate characterization of the instantaneous signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) is important for reliability-sensitive cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) systems. This paper proposes a joint estimation method for link-specific large-scale fading coefficients (LSFCs) and a common Nakagami-m shape parameter using power and downlink SINR measurements. A tractable SINR distribution is first derived under global zero-forcing (GZF) precoding, Nakagami-m fading, and link-level fractional power control (FPC). Based on the derived probability density function (PDF), a model-driven neural network (NN) is developed to solve the resulting maximum-likelihood estimation (MLE) problem. Simulations show that the reconstructed SINR distributions obtained with the estimated parameters closely match the empirical distributions. With 2 ×10⁵ samples, the proposed method achieves an LSFC root-mean-square error (RMSE) of approximately 1.0 dB and an m RMSE of approximately 0.085.

entries.title: Prop-WRF: Proposal-Guided Wireless Radiance Field for Scalable Multi-Frequency Outdoor Channel Frequency Response Prediction
entries.abstract: Sparse-directional wireless radiance fields (WRFs) enable complex channel frequency response (CFR) prediction from receiver locations and multipath direction priors. However, in large-scale outdoor environments, long sampling intervals make it difficult to concentrate a limited sampling budget around valid virtual anchors (VAs), degrading prediction accuracy and training stability. This paper proposes Prop-WRF, a proposalnetwork-guided WRF for CFR prediction across multiple subcarriers. A lightweight proposal network learns VA occupancy densities through online distillation from the main network and iteratively guides resampling toward likely VA locations. The main network then predicts complex radiance over the refined intervals and synthesizes CFRs using an analytical propagation model. By introducing frequency encoding only into the radiance branch, a single model jointly learns shared VA geometry from observations across subcarriers while representing frequencydependent complex radiance. A stage-wise hybrid normalized loss and an interval-weight regularizer further strengthen weakchannel supervision and suppress spurious VA peaks. In addition, a multipath simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) front end refines receiver states and path associations to construct geometrically consistent training priors. Simulations show that Prop-WRF improves CFR prediction accuracy and training stability over conventional sparse-directional WRF baselines in larger environments.

entries.title: Sparse Range-Doppler Profile Recovery in Colored Interference for Adaptive Radar
entries.abstract: Range-Doppler profile (RDP) recovery is a fundamental task in adaptive radar signal processing, whose performance can be severely degraded by Doppler grid mismatch and colored interference. This article develops a unified sparsity-aware framework for on-grid and off-grid RDP recovery in the presence of correlated clutter with unknown spectral properties. The problem is formulated within a regularized maximum likelihood framework by exploiting both primary and secondary data, where the sparse RDP and interference covariance are jointly inferred, while Doppler frequency displacements are additionally estimated in the off-grid case to mitigate basis mismatch. Both covariance-adaptive one-step formulations and their sample-covariance-matrix-based two-step alternatives are developed within the mentioned framework. The resulting challenging nonconvex optimization problems are efficiently tackled by a majorization-minimization (MM) algorithm for the on-grid case and an MM-minimum block improvement (MBI) approach for the off-grid counterpart. Furthermore, Bayesian information criterion (BIC)-based refinement strategies are introduced to improve RDP recovery and Doppler frequency displacement estimation. Numerical results under colored interference demonstrate the superior recovery performance of the proposed methods over representative benchmarks.

entries.title: Karhunen-Loève Transforms of Autoregressive Windows Based on Matched Symmetry Groups
entries.abstract: The Karhunen-Loève transform of a window of a stationary autoregressive process of any order p is described through its poles, extending the Algebraic Diversity framework, which selects a transform by the matched group. For simple roots every basis vector is a sum of at most p sinusoids, at the frequencies where the spectrum equals the eigenvalue, plus modes decaying from the ends. The window covariance differs from a member of the class diagonalized by the type-II discrete cosine transform by a closed-form matrix of rank 2p, exactly when no pole is zero, so the eigenvalues interlace spectrum samples on the cosine grid, and the coding-gain loss of the cosine transform is an exact function of that matrix with computable bounds: for the 8×8 Markov block of image coding at pole 0.95 it is below 1.2 percent. By Kronecker's theorem the rank is at most 2max(p,q) for rational spectra; a moving-average window departs in its Hankel corners, and an integrated (ARIMA) window departs by low rank from the type-VII sine class, exact for the random walk. The exact symmetry is generically the reflection and contains a wreath product for interleaved windows; the dihedral group of the even extension is matched approximately, the dominant pole's sign choosing cosine or sine. The two groups give the transform a fast form: a parity fold, half-length cosine cores and a cascade of at most p first-order Cauchy stages, exactly p for a minimal AR(p) model. The first-order case recovers results obtained by other means.
entries.comment: v1: 38 pages, 7 figures

entries.title: Descriptor: UWB Anchor Self-Calibration Dataset (UWB-ASC)
entries.abstract: Anchor self-calibration estimates the positions of fixed nodes of an indoor radio positioning or localization system from observations among the nodes and to mobile devices. It replaces the survey of every anchor, which is costly and goes stale when anchors move. The UWB Anchor Self-Calibration Dataset (UWB-ASC) is a testing ground for such methods, recorded in one industrial hall with ultra-wideband (UWB) two-way ranging. It has three parts. The first is two measured deployments. In the line-of-sight (LOS) deployment, 10 anchors range with a walking tag tracked by motion capture.
